data.description:
## Description

**What**: Create `plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/aws-status.sh` emitting a single JSON document with one explicit entry per telemetry resource. Create `plugins/dso/scripts/telemetry/aws-teardown.sh` removing all telemetry AWS resources, gated by an explicit `--user-approved` flag (exits 1 without it).
**Why**: `aws-status.sh` closes the idempotency-verification half of sc-1 (the JSON summary check). `aws-teardown.sh` prevents accidental data loss during development.
**Scope**:
- IN: Status reporter with 5-resource JSON output, teardown gate, stable JSON schema.
- OUT: Provisioning (aws-setup-bucket.sh, aws-setup-lambda.sh). Handler code.

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, running `aws-status.sh` against a deployed telemetry stack emits a single JSON document with one explicit entry per resource: (1) bucket (name, lifecycle tier=Glacier-IR, public-access-block enabled, SSE enabled), (2) Lambda function (name, Function URL, reserved-concurrency setting), (3) IAM execution role (name, trust policy includes lambda.amazonaws.com), (4) CloudWatch log group (name, retention=7d), (5) operational metrics (last-24h event count).
  ← Satisfies: sc-1  (sc-1: "aws-status.sh returns JSON summary of all five resources")
- When this story is complete, the JSON schema of `aws-status.sh` output is stable (documented) so downstream health-check scripts can consume it without parsing drift.
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, running `aws-teardown.sh` without `--user-approved` exits 1 with a clear message; with `--user-approved` it removes the Lambda, execution role, S3 bucket, and CloudWatch log group.
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, running `aws-status.sh` after successful teardown reports all five resources as absent without throwing a non-zero exit code.
  ← Satisfies: sc-1

## Considerations

- [Safety] `aws-teardown.sh` is destructive; require `--user-approved` AND print a confirmation summary of what will be deleted before proceeding.
- [JSON contract] `aws-status.sh` output schema should be versioned/stable; downstream scripts must not break on whitespace or key-order changes.
- [Config dependency] Both scripts read resource names from `dso-config.conf` `review_telemetry.*` keys written by aws-setup-bucket.sh and aws-setup-lambda.sh.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As an operator, I want aws-status.sh to report a JSON summary of all five telemetry resources and aws-teardown.sh to clean-uninstall behind a --user-approved gate.
